The Labour Department announced today (the 10th) that Waso Cafe (Prince Edward) provided false information to the department during the local open recruitment period when applying to import foreign labour, and has been imposed with administrative sanctions by the department, including immediately suspending the company's application and refusing to process the company's applications within the following year. Related report: Importing Foreign Labour｜What were the reasons for the 18 cases of administrative sanctions? Received 1,365 complaints in three years, approximately one-tenth received warnings or administrative sanctions

Waso Cafe (Prince Edward) has been administratively sanctioned by the Labour Department for providing false information during the local open recruitment period.

A spokesperson for the Labour Department pointed out that after investigation, it was confirmed that Waso Cafe (Prince Edward) provided false information during the local open recruitment period for applying to import waiters, junior cooks and dishwashers, violating the regulations of the "Enhanced Supplementary Labour Programme", and therefore was imposed with administrative sanctions. The department has immediately suspended the company's submitted application for importing foreign labour, and refused to process the company's applications submitted under the Enhanced Programme within the following year.

The department emphasised that employers importing foreign labour must strictly comply with the regulations of the programme, including prioritising the employment of suitable local workers. If employers violate labour or immigration laws, the regulations of the Enhanced Programme or the standard employment contract, the Labour Department will impose administrative sanctions, including suspending the employer's submitted applications, revoking the employer's approved import labour quotas, and refusing to process the employer's subsequently submitted applications.

Including Waso Cafe (Prince Edward), whose sanctions were just announced today, FactWire has compiled information on 18 companies penalised for violating import foreign labour regulations. Among them, 10 companies belong to the catering services and cleaning industries. What were the reasons for their penalties? Among the 18 companies, 9 were involved in unreasonably refusing to hire local job seekers, with most being refused to process their applications for importing foreign labour for the following two years by the Labour Department; another two restaurants dismissed local employees after importing foreign labour, and had their already approved foreign labour approvals revoked immediately.
